To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the high-throughput approach has enabled us to discover and characterize novel materials with improved properties.

We have demonstrated that high throughput combinatorial tools can be used to investigate the properties of transparent conducting oxides (such as In Zn O) and other thin films (such as In Ti O and In Mo O).
we have demonstrated that combinatorial approaches can be used to obtain new TCOs with improved properties for photovoltaic applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel transparent conducting oxides (ITO and AZO) and high performance antireflective coatings (TiO2 and ZnO).
the development of new materials, devices and processes for photovoltaic applications.
the development of new materials for solar cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the high throughput approach is a very useful tool to investigate and optimize the properties of thin films for photovoltaic applications, and in particular for the development of new transparent conducting oxides.
the combinatorial high-throughput approach is a powerful and effective tool for the rapid screening of materials for solar cell application.
the combinatorial high through put tools are a valuable tool to study the properties of thin film solar cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ITO is the best TCO for low temperature processing and ITiO is the best TNO for high performance.
the highest mobilities are obtained for ITiO and IMO deposited at 550C.
the best performance is obtained for IZO and ITiO deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high throughput techniques are very useful to screen a large number of compositions and to find new materials that have interesting properties.
the use of combinatorial techniques can accelerate the development of new materials and provide a more efficient approach to materials screening.
high mobility TCOs are possible at low temperatures.
